\chapter{Learning Theory — Convex Minimax Core}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.ConvexMinimaxCore
\section{Overview}

This module develops the core ingredients for the convex-compact minimax theorem,
following Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi Theorem~7.1 specialized to subsets of~$\bbr$.
It provides the exact minimax value for finite matrix games (derived from the
Hedge approximate saddle-point theorem), Jensen-type inequalities for
mixed-strategy convex combinations, a sampled-game construction that bridges
finite and continuous settings, and the compactness machinery (sublevel sets,
finite-intersection property) needed for the infinite-dimensional direction.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Arbitrary mixed strategy]
\lean{OnlineLearning.arbitraryMixedStrategy}
\label{OnlineLearning.arbitraryMixedStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
Given $n \geq 1$, \texttt{OnlineLearning.arbitraryMixedStrategy} is a concrete
element of $\mathrm{MixedStrategy}(n)$ that places all probability mass on a
single arbitrarily chosen action. It is used solely to witness that the type
of mixed strategies is nonempty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lower value of a finite game]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure}
For a finite zero-sum game $G$ with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions,
the \emph{lower value} is
\[
  v^- (G) \;=\; \sup_{p \in \Delta_M}\; \inf_{j \in [N]}\; \mathrm{payoffVsPure}(G,p,j),
\]
where the row player maximises over mixed strategies and the column player
minimises over pure responses.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Upper value of a finite game]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, pureVsPayoff}
The \emph{upper value} of $G$ is
\[
  v^+(G) \;=\; \inf_{q \in \Delta_N}\; \sup_{i \in [M]}\; \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G,i,q),
\]
where the column player minimises over mixed strategies and the row player
maximises over pure responses.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the mixed payoff against a pure column]
\lean{OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_nonneg}
\label{OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, let $p$ be a mixed row strategy over the $M$ rows, and let $j$ be a pure column
action. Then the expected payoff of $p$ against column $j$ is non-negative:
\[
  \sum_{i} p_i \cdot A_{ij} \;\ge\; 0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expected payoff against a pure column is at most one]
\lean{OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_le_one}
\label{OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game whose payoff matrix $A$ has every entry in
$[0,1]$, let $p$ be a mixed row strategy with weights $p_i$, and let $j$ be a fixed pure
column action. Then the row player's expected payoff against column $j$ satisfies \[
\sum_i p_i \cdot A_{ij} \;\le\; 1. \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of a pure row's expected payoff]
\lean{OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_nonneg}
\label{OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, whose payoff matrix $A$ has entries satisfying $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$. Fix a pure
row action $i$ and a mixed column strategy $q$, so its weights $q_j$ are non-negative
and sum to $1$. Then the expected payoff of row $i$ against $q$ is non-negative:
\[
  \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j \;\ge\; 0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pure row payoff against a mixed column is at most one]
\lean{OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_le_one}
\label{OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, whose payoff matrix $A$ satisfies $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$ for all entries, and let
$q$ be a mixed column strategy, that is, a probability distribution $q_1, \dots, q_N$
over the columns. Then for every pure row action $i$, the expected payoff of row $i$
against $q$ satisfies
\[
  \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j \;\le\; 1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Row player's guaranteed payoffs are bounded above]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_bddAbove}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_bddAbove}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_le_one, OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_nonneg, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N \ge 1$ column
actions, whose payoff matrix $(A_{ij})$ satisfies $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$ for all $i,j$.
For a mixed row strategy $p = (p_i)$ over the $M$ rows, let $L(p) = \inf_{j} \sum_i p_i
A_{ij}$ be the least expected payoff against a pure column, taken over all $N$ columns.
Then the set $\{\, L(p) : p \text{ is a mixed strategy over the rows} \,\}$ is bounded
above.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lower boundedness of the row-supremum values]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue_bddBelow}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue_bddBelow}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_le_one, OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_nonneg, ZeroSumGame, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, whose payoff matrix $A$ satisfies $A_{ij} \in [0,1]$ for all $i,j$. For a mixed
column strategy $q$ (a probability distribution on the $N$ columns), let
\[
  v(q) \;=\; \sup_{i}\, \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j
\]
be the best expected payoff that a single pure row can achieve against $q$. Then the set
$\{\, v(q) : q \text{ a mixed column strategy}\,\}$ is bounded below.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weak duality for finite zero-sum games]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_le_upperValue}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_le_upperValue}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue, ZeroSumGame, weak_duality}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \geq 1$ row actions and $N \geq 1$
column actions, given by a payoff matrix $A_{ij} \in [0,1]$ that the row player seeks to
maximise and the column player to minimise. Then the lower value never exceeds the upper
value:
\[
  \sup_{p \in \Delta_M}\; \min_{j}\; \sum_{i} p_i A_{ij}
  \;\;\leq\;\;
  \inf_{q \in \Delta_N}\; \max_{i}\; \sum_{j} A_{ij} q_j,
\]
where $\Delta_M$ and $\Delta_N$ denote the sets of mixed strategies (probability
distributions) over the row and column actions, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Minimax theorem for finite zero-sum games]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finite_minimax_value}
\label{OnlineLearning.finite_minimax_value}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_bddAbove, OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue_le_upperValue, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue_bddBelow, OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_le_one, ZeroSumGame, approx_minimax, payoffVsPure, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, whose payoff matrix $A = (A_{ij})$ satisfies $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$ for all
$i,j$. Suppose $M > 1$ and $N \ge 1$. Then the lower and upper values of $G$ coincide:
\[
  \sup_{p \in \Delta_M}\; \inf_{j \in [N]}\; \sum_{i} p_i\, A_{ij}
  \;=\;
  \inf_{q \in \Delta_N}\; \sup_{i \in [M]}\; \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j,
\]
where $\Delta_M$ and $\Delta_N$ denote the sets of mixed strategies (probability
distributions) over the row and column actions respectively.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Convex-compact minimax statement]
\lean{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement}
\label{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement}
\leanok
For sets $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and a payoff function $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$,
\texttt{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement} is the proposition
\[
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y}\,f(x,y)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X}\,f(x,y).
\]
It is packaged as a named \texttt{Prop} so that intermediate lemmas can refer
to it while the proof is built up incrementally.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Convex-compact minimax hypotheses]
\lean{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses}
\label{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses}
\leanok
A structure bundling the assumptions of Cesa-Bianchi--Lugosi Theorem~7.1
for $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ on sets $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$: both sets
are nonempty, $X$ is compact and convex, $Y$ is convex, $f(\cdot,y)$ is
continuous and convex on $X$ for every $y \in Y$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is concave on
$Y$ for every $x \in X$, and $f$ is bounded above and below on $X \times Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Convex sets are closed under mixed-strategy averages]
\lean{OnlineLearning.mixed_sum_mem_convex}
\label{OnlineLearning.mixed_sum_mem_convex}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set, let $p$ be a mixed strategy over $n$ actions
with weights $p_1, \dots, p_n \ge 0$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i = 1$, and let $x_1,
\dots, x_n \in S$. Then the weighted average $\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\, x_i$ again lies in
$S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen's inequality for a mixed strategy]
\lean{OnlineLearning.convexOn_mixed_sum_le}
\label{OnlineLearning.convexOn_mixed_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set and let $g : \bbr \to \bbr$ be convex on $S$. Let
$p$ be a mixed strategy over $n$ actions, that is, a family of weights $p_1, \dots, p_n
\ge 0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i = 1$, and let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be points of $S$. Then
\[
  g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\, x_i\right)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\, g(x_i).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen's inequality for a concave function]
\lean{OnlineLearning.concaveOn_le_mixed_sum}
\label{OnlineLearning.concaveOn_le_mixed_sum}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ and let $g : \bbr \to \bbr$ be concave on $S$. Let $p = (p_1,
\dots, p_n)$ be a mixed strategy over $n$ actions, that is, a tuple of weights $p_j \ge
0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{n} p_j = 1$, and let $y_1, \dots, y_n$ be points of $S$. Then
\[
  \sum_{j=1}^{n} p_j\, g(y_j) \;\le\; g\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n} p_j\, y_j\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Sampled finite game]
\lean{OnlineLearning.sampledGame}
\label{OnlineLearning.sampledGame}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame}
Given a payoff function $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ with values in $[0,1]$,
finite families of row points $x : [M] \to \bbr$ and column points
$y : [N] \to \bbr$, the \emph{sampled game} is the $M\times N$ matrix game
whose $(i,j)$ entry is $f(x_i, y_j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minimax theorem for a sampled finite game]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finite_sampled_minimax_value}
\label{OnlineLearning.finite_sampled_minimax_value}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue, OnlineLearning.finite_minimax_value, OnlineLearning.sampledGame}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and let $x : [M] \to \bbr$ and $y
: [N] \to \bbr$ be finite families of row and column points such that $0 \le f(x_i, y_j)
\le 1$ for all $i$ and $j$. Suppose the column action set is nonempty ($N \ge 1$) and
there are at least two row actions ($M \ge 2$). Then the sampled game — the $M \times N$
matrix game with entries $f(x_i, y_j)$ — has equal lower and upper values,
\[
  \sup_{p \in \Delta_M}\; \inf_{j \in [N]}\; \sum_{i} p_i\, f(x_i, y_j)
  \;=\;
  \inf_{q \in \Delta_N}\; \sup_{i \in [M]}\; \sum_{j} f(x_i, y_j)\, q_j,
\]
where $\Delta_M$ and $\Delta_N$ denote the sets of mixed strategies over the row and
column actions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bound for the sampled payoff against a pure column]
\lean{OnlineLearning.sampled_payoffVsPure_ge_convex_combo}
\label{OnlineLearning.sampled_payoffVsPure_ge_convex_combo}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, OnlineLearning.convexOn_mixed_sum_le, OnlineLearning.sampledGame, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ take values in $[0,1]$, and let $x : [M] \to \bbr$ and
$y : [N] \to \bbr$ be finite families of row and column points, giving rise to the
sampled game whose $(i,j)$ entry is $f(x_i, y_j)$. Fix a column index $j$, and suppose
the section $x' \mapsto f(x', y_j)$ is convex on a set $X \subseteq \bbr$ with $x_i \in
X$ for every $i$. Then for any mixed row strategy $p$ over the $M$ rows,
\[
  f\!\left(\sum_{i} p_i\, x_i,\; y_j\right) \;\le\; \sum_{i} p_i\, f(x_i, y_j),
\]
where the right-hand side is the expected payoff of the sampled game against column $j$
under $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concavity bound on sampled payoff against a mixed column]
\lean{OnlineLearning.sampled_pureVsPayoff_le_concave_combo}
\label{OnlineLearning.sampled_pureVsPayoff_le_concave_combo}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, OnlineLearning.concaveOn_le_mixed_sum, OnlineLearning.sampledGame, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f:\bbr\times\bbr\to\bbr$ be a payoff function taking values in $[0,1]$, and let
$x:[M]\to\bbr$ and $y:[N]\to\bbr$ be finite families of row and column points. Fix a row
index $i$ and a mixed column strategy $q$, whose weights $q_j\ge 0$ sum to $1$. Suppose
$Y\subseteq\bbr$ contains every $y_j$ and the section $y'\mapsto f(x_i,y')$ is concave
on $Y$. Then the expected payoff of pure row $i$ against $q$ in the sampled game is at
most the value of $f$ at the $q$-averaged column point:
\[
  \sum_{j} f(x_i,y_j)\, q_j \;\le\; f\!\left(x_i,\; \sum_{j} q_j\, y_j\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weak minimax inequality for convex-compact games]
\lean{OnlineLearning.weak_convex_compact_minimax}
\label{OnlineLearning.weak_convex_compact_minimax}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ be nonempty convex sets with $X$ also compact, and let $f : X
\times Y \to \bbr$ be a payoff that is bounded above and below on $X \times Y$, such
that for every $y \in Y$ the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous and convex on $X$, and
for every $x \in X$ the map $y \mapsto f(x,y)$ is concave on $Y$. Then
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X}\, f(x,y)
  \;\leq\;
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y}\, f(x,y).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Minimax sublevel set]
\lean{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel}
\label{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel}
\leanok
For a set $X \subseteq \bbr$, a payoff function $f$, a column point $y$, and
a threshold $c \in \bbr$, the \emph{minimax sublevel set} is
\[
  \mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) \;=\; X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \leq c\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Minimax sublevel set is contained in the row set]
\lean{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_subset}
\label{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_subset}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X \subseteq \bbr$ be a set, let $f \colon \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff
function, and let $y, c \in \bbr$. Then the minimax sublevel set
$\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \leq c\}$ is contained in
$X$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Closedness of the minimax sublevel set]
\lean{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isClosed}
\label{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isClosed}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel}
\difficulty{2}
Let $X \subseteq \bbr$ be a closed set, let $f\colon \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be a
payoff function, and fix a column point $y \in \bbr$ and a threshold $c \in \bbr$. If
the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous on $X$, then the minimax sublevel set
$\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \le c\}$ is closed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compactness of a minimax sublevel set]
\lean{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isCompact}
\label{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isCompact}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isClosed, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_subset}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X \subseteq \bbr$ be compact, fix a payoff function $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to
\bbr$, a column point $y \in \bbr$, and a threshold $c \in \bbr$, and suppose the map $x
\mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous on $X$. Then the minimax sublevel set
$\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \le c\}$ is compact.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[From finite feasibility to a uniform row point]
\lean{OnlineLearning.exists_forall_le_of_finite_sublevel_intersections}
\label{OnlineLearning.exists_forall_le_of_finite_sublevel_intersections}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel_isClosed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ together with a payoff function $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$
satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, and let $c \in \bbr$. Suppose that for
every finite subset $u \subseteq Y$ the set $X \cap \bigcap_{y \in u}
\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c)$ is nonempty, where $\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x
\in \bbr : f(x,y) \le c\}$; that is, there is a common row point $x \in X$ with $f(x,y)
\le c$ for all $y$ in that finite set. Then there exists a single $x \in X$ with $f(x,y)
\le c$ for every $y \in Y$.
\end{lemma}
